content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore office document formats within XML in Real-World Data Formats. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XML is a family of syntaxes and vocabularies used in practical formats. A file may be one part of a larger package, and its namespace, packaging rules, and host application semantics all matter.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Open XML document packages; XML inside Office file formats; Relationships between package parts; Inspecting structured document content. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Office Document Formats
content_blocks.expected_output: Office document formats often store several XML parts inside a package; a single XML part is not the entire Office file.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Inspect the format specification and a minimal valid sample. Do not assume that every XML-based format can be opened as a standalone XML document or edited without preserving package metadata.
